handoff: GitLab draft MRs come back titled 'Draft: …', so the first sync after open-pr retitles every one to the bare issue title, which also removes its draft status (blocking F1). gh path, decide rule and tests are fine; tests and typecheck green.

findings.title: GitLab draft MRs are retitled at the first sync, which removes their draft status
findings.criterion: RemotePort editPullRequestTitle and RemotePullRequest.title hold for gh, glab and FakeRemote
findings.detail:
GitLab keeps a merge request's draft state in its title: `glab mr create --draft` (packages/adapters/src/glab/index.ts:210) opens the MR as `Draft: <title>`, and GitLab's REST and GraphQL `title` fields return the prefix. mapMr (glab/index.ts:89) and restMr (:126) pass that title through unchanged. So retitlePr compares `Draft: Count items` with the issue's `Count items`, sees a mismatch on every open draft MR, and emits retitle_pr. `glab mr update --title 'Count items'` then drops the prefix, and GitLab marks the MR ready. Every story MR on GitLab leaves draft at the first sync after open-pr, whether or not the issue was renamed. The glab fixtures (glab/fixtures/calls.json:116, :164) and scriptedGlab's mrJson show `draft: true` with an unprefixed title, so no test catches it.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: In the glab adapter, report the title without a leading `Draft:`, `[Draft]`, `(Draft)` or `WIP:` prefix. In editPullRequestTitle, keep the prefix when the MR is a draft, for example by passing `--draft` with `--title` to glab. Add a glab fixture with a real `Draft: ` title. Also add a decide or contract case: a draft MR whose title matches the issue apart from the provider's prefix emits no retitle.

findings.title: A failed retitle overwrites the story unit's act failure, and a later successful retitle never clears it
findings.detail:
retitle_pr goes through recordFailure as an ordinary unit action, so a failure writes failures[storyKey] with effect `retitle_pr`. It runs after the unit's own action, so on a tick where that action's push or commit was refused, the retitle failure replaces the refused push or commit. A refused push stays an Unblock item until it succeeds; the retitle failure that replaces it disappears on agent activity. retitlePr (lifecycle.ts:249) also never adds to act.effectsOk, so a later successful retitle leaves the Unblock item from the earlier failure in place until the cursor moves. push_record keeps its own slot for exactly this reason (recordPushFailure).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Give retitle_pr its own failure slot, as recordPushFailure does, or skip recording it (the next sync retries it), and add `retitle_pr` to effectsOk on success.
